The North Quays main contract has made signifi cant progress in the last two 
months.  The substructure works for the Sustainable Transport Bridge is 
continuing with all four cofferdams operational and work progressing internally 
with the formation of the bridge piers.  The fabrication of the steel deck 
superstructure in Belgium is close to completion, the sections are currently being 
painted.  The pile support slab for the South Plaza is well progressed with over 
half of the concrete slab now poured.    
South Plaza area and bridge cofferdams  
The Transport Hub building works is continuing with the support walls and 
columns complete and the construction of the southern platform blockwork at 
platform level has commenced.  Construction of the northern platform reinforced 
boundary wall is ongoing.  Works to external lift shafts are proceeding to roof 
level.   
Transport hub, viewed from Fountain Street
Demolition of Hump bank bridge / OBH 127 to allow for western pedestrian bridge 
construction Road and access infrastructure is also progressing well, with works 
continuing on the various bridge structures.  The humpback bridge / OBH 127 
was demolished in late May to allow for the pedestrian bridge construction. The 
western access bridge is near completion and the decks for the greenway 
underpasses are well advanced.    
Pump Station  
Uisce Eireann is now operating the new pump station in Ferrybank.   
Flood Defence Scheme 
Site investigations and detailed design are progressing well and construction works are programmed to commence in 
Q3 2024. 
Western Access bridge (Bridge S19) substantially complete 
Traffi c management measures continue to be in place, with works continuing along Fountain Street and will be 
progressing to Abbey Road in July.  The installation / upgrading of the foul sewer on Abbey Road necessitates the 
closure of Abbey Road for a seven week period.  This work has been scheduled over the summer months to minimise 
disruption.  Local and pedestrian access to this area is being facilitated throughout the works.

Waterford Rural Tourism Network 
The Waterford Rural Tourism Network (WRTN), is continuing to develop. Since the beginning of 2024 the following have 
been delivered by Runda Hospitality: Networking events, Online & in-person meetings, First of 5  Learning Journeys, FI 
Programmes, B2C workshops. There is much more planned for delivery by the end of 2024.
DEDP Implementation Group
As the Waterford Destination & Experience Development Plan (DEDP) nears completion a stakeholder Implementation 
Group has been established to ensure the tourism industry has a clear voice in the delivery of actions and projects 
identified in the plan. Two in-person meetings have taken place to date.

A new 6 part series being filmed in Ireland for broadcast on PBS in the US has commenced filming in Waterford. We can

These images will be shared through Tourism Ireland in the Canada and through local channels too.

North Quays Strategic Development Zone
Hopcast Limited submitted a planning application to Waterford City and County Council on the 5th June for a major 
mixed-use development on the North Quays Strategic Development Zone (Planning Ref: 2460304).
The proposed mixed-use development would comprise the fi rst phase of the development of the SDZ lands. The 
proposal includes 9 blocks with a total gross fl oor area (GFA) of 60,579sqm (64,953sqm including under croft and
basement car parks (4,374sqm)). The proposed development would involve the construction of a podium to establish 
a new ground/ street formation level to connect to the Sustainable Transport Bridge (by WCCC) at the Central Plaza. 
Provision is made for pedestrian connection from Central Plaza to Dock Road via the approved pedestrian bridge (by 
WCCC). A new riverside promenade / cycleway (part of Greenway) is proposed between the Sustainable Transport 
Bridge and the Eastern Access to the site. The proposed blocks would comprise a hotel, an aparthotel, six blocks of 
apartments (with retail and restaurant/café use at ground fl oor level) and an offi ce block at the eastern end of the site.
Full details of the proposal can be viewed online at: https://www.eplanning.ie/WaterfordCCC/AppFileRefDe-
tails/2460304/0. In addition, there is a paper copy of the application (and all the supporting documentation) which is 
available for inspection in the Planning Offi ce.This planning application is due to be decided by the 30th of July 2024.  
The last date for third party submission in relation to this proposal is Tuesday 9th July 2024.

LAND MANAGEMENT AND DERELICT SITES TEAM

RURAL VACANCY AND DERELICTION FUND
The active land management team was successful in putting a business plan together for a €1M (max of 10 properties 
at any one time) Rural Vacancy and Dereliction Fund {RVDF} to tackle long term vacant and derelict properties in 
Waterford’s rural settlements. 
It is envisaged that the RVDF will tackle properties that have been long term vacant and derelict within the centre of 
our rural settlements and bring them back into active use - predominately for residential use - for re-sale on the private 
market. 
The RVDF Fund will act as a much broader tool for the activation of long term vacant and derelict buildings which may 
not be appropriate or suitable for social housing schemes. It will also focus on tackling properties which are either not on 
the market for sale or to which the market has not responded in order to prevent unnecessary interventions and mitigate 
against any risk of adding to property price inflation.
RVDF involves a whole of local authority approach – planning, housing, property, finance, economic development. The 
RVDF Fund will integrate with wider regeneration initiatives and programmes that are underway. These include actions 
related to the implementation of the Town Centre First policy and the work of Town Regeneration Officers where 
appropriate, as well as through funding supports like the Croi Conaithe {Towns) Fund and SEAi grant schemes for long 
term vacant or derelict properties.

CPO ACTIVATION PROGRAMME
The Department of Housing, Local Government and Heritage (the Department) released the CPO activation programme 
for local authorities last year.  Under the Programme, there was an overall target of 4,000 properties to enter the Activa-
tion Programme in 2023 and a target for the compulsory purchases / compulsory acquisitions to commence in relation 
to 400 properties. The Programme set individual targets for each local authority for 2023. They set a target for Waterford 
City and County Council of:
	
•75 vacant and derelict properties to enter the Programme, and 
	
•40 compulsory purchases / compulsory acquisitions to commence. 
The Department is now preparing to publish the CPO Activation Programme 2023 Progress Report. This report will 
show that Waterford City and County Council:
	
•entered 157 properties into the CPO Activation Programme in 2023 and 
	
•that 25 compulsory purchases / compulsory acquisitions commenced. 
The Department has released the national targets for 2024. Following a review of progress in 2023, new overall targets 
are proposed of:
	
•3,500 properties to enter the Programme in 2024, and 
	
•250 compulsory purchases / compulsory acquisitions to commence.
The lower 2024 targets reflect the fact that the properties to enter the CPO Activation Programme in 2024 are in addition 
to many of the properties which entered in 2023, with work ongoing in relation to these by local authorities.
In relation to Waterford City and County Council, it is proposed that the following targets be set for 2024: 
	
•100 properties to enter the CPO Activation Programme, and 
	
•30 compulsory purchases / compulsory acquisitions to commence.

Forward Planning July 2024 Plenary ReportnResidential Zoned Land Tax (RZLT) Draft Annual Revised Map
On the 1st of February last, Waterford City and County Council prepared and published the RZLT draft annual revised 
map for the 2025 tax liability year where the following general timeline applies to the annual mapping process:
1.	
Publication of a draft annual revised map followed by a 2-month period of public consultation, accompanied by 
placement of advertisements in local press and across Waterford Council social media accounts;
2.	
Receipt of written submissions from landowners and consideration thereof;
3.	
Notification of written determinations made by Waterford Council to the relevant landowners who made written 
submissions to the draft map;
4.	
Making of appeals to An Bord Pleanála where landowners are aggrieved by the determination of the council;
5.	
Publication of final annual revised map at the start of the relevant tax liability year followed by a repeat of the 
process to prepare a new draft annual revised map. 
We have now completed stages 1 – 3 in the timeline. During the consultation period a total of 14 written submissions 
were received through the consult.waterfordcouncil.ie portal. We have now responded to each of the written submis-
sions and the relevant landowners may appeal our determinations to An Bord Pleanála during July. A total of 3 submis-
sions sought to have lands rezoned by way of variation to the development plan however we have not supported such 
requests. The final annual map will be published early 2025 having regard to the determinations of both the planning 
authority and those of An Bord Pleanála.

plan report will be accompanied by the 2-year Strategic Environmental Assessment monitoring report with both docu-
ments proposed for circulation to the plenary council in September. The reports should inform further discussion with 
both the planning SPC and the plenary council on any changes required to support full implementation of the plan. 
Biodiversity Officer Report
The Waterford Biodiversity Action Plan will be developed by the WCCC Biodiversity Officer, Marina Mulligan. The pro-
cess is in the very early stages of development to identify stakeholders and gather existing actions present in regional, 
national, EU and international plans which will be integrated with the BAP for Waterford. This process will continue over 
the course of 2024 and into early 2025.  The action to create a Local Authority Biodiversity Action Plan sits under the 
actions laid out in the 4th National Biodiversity Action Plan. It will include stages for preparation, development, draft and 
public consultation, before publication in 2025.  Once developed, this document will guide the local authority on imple-
mentation of actions for biodiversity across the county and include collaboration with numerous organisations, commu-
nities and members of the public.

COMMUNITY GRANTS
Waterford City and County Council at its plenary meeting on 14th March, approved 288 allocations under the Supporting 
Waterford Communities Fund 2024, totalling €241,430. Successful applicants received Letters of Offer and payments 
have been processed. Projects must be completed by 25th November 2024. 
The Local Enhancement Programme (LEP) is funded by the Department of Rural and Community Development and is 
administered by Waterford Local Community Development Committee (LCDC) / WCCC. On March 14th, the Waterford 
LCDC approved 164 allocations under the LEP 2024 General Fund, totalling €153,405.12 and a further 26 allocations, 
totalling €31,824.28, were ringfenced under the Women’s Fund.  Letters of Offer have issued to all successful applicants. 
Once projects are completed, receipts and photographs must be provided by the groups to receive their respective allo-
cations. Projects must be complete by 20th September 2024. 
The Community Recognition Fund 2024 was launched by Minister Heather Humphreys on 15th March. Waterford City & 
County Council received eighteen (18) applications under window 1, Seven (7) applications were put forward for consid-
eration to the Department of Rural and Community Development, totalling €491,392.  Once finalised, details of the fund 
will be included on the Council’s website and communicated via the PPN and the Council’s social media platforms.
LEADER 2023-2027
Seven (7) projects that were recommended by the Evaluation Committee under the first targeted call, were approved by 
the LCDC/LAG and Letters of Offer issued. Further applications were due on 10th May 2024 and fourteen (14) projects 
were received. The Evaluation Committee will meet in July to assess these applications.
LEADER 2014-2022
One project remains to be completed in the LEADER 2014/2022 Programme; an extension is being arranged to facilitate 
completion.
AFRICA DAY 2024
Africa Day Waterford which took place in the Cultural Quarter on the 25th of May, marked the tenth anniversary of Africa 
Day in Waterford. Despite inclement weather the atmosphere was vibrant. 21 stalls were in place with a diverse mix of 
foods, arts, crafts, clothing, hair braiding, henna painting, and jewellery. Two music stages provided 4 hours of 
entertainment and a variety of cultural dances took place.  Active Cities provided on street games for children and the 
Nore Valley Farm petting zoo was a popular attraction. International cooperation via 23 Irish embassies and growing trade 
links between Ireland and Africa were noted in speeches by Council officials and representatives of the African community. 
AGE WELL EXPO 
Waterford’s first Age Well Expo took place in the Tower Hotel on May 7th, and throughout the afternoon was attended by 
over 1,500 participants.
The Age Friendly Waterford event, in association with Healthy Waterford, UPMC Whitfield and Waterford City and County 
Council showcased the services, supports and activities available to older people to lead fulfilling, healthy and active lives. 
The expo featured talks from keynote speakers and interviews with local organisations and community groups providing 
insightful and topical information to everyone who strives to age well.  
Over 50 exhibition stands were present on the day including, An Garda Síochána, Waterford and Wexford Education and 
Training Board, HSE, SETU Lifelong Learning, ALONE, Waterford Volunteer Centre, Waterford Libraries, Fire Services, 
Waterford Sports Partnership and Local Link, along with speakers from Waterford Integrated Care for Older People and 
SETU on returning to education.  Waterford City and County Council also showcased support services available, such as 
housing grants, community engagement initiatives, energy cost reduction, recreational activities tailored for older adults 
and more.

CONNECTING COMMUNITY ROADSHOWS 
The Connecting Community Roadshows were a series of seven collaborative, cross organisational roadshows which 
took place from February through to May. These roadshows involved over 30 agencies visiting rural and urban locations 
throughout the county, with an aim to promote the best Waterford has to offer in community services.   
The workshops took place in all of Waterford’s municipal districts and offered an opportunity for engagement with a variety 
of stakeholders on the day. They also provided insight and guidance about setting up community groups, sourcing funding 
for developing community initiatives and how to build a stronger, inclusive, and vibrant place to live. 
A review meeting took place on the 28th of May to gain feedback from partners, review effectives and build on lessons 
learned.  All feedback received was extremely positive, as was a willingness by all parties to continue into 2025.  Attend-
ees at the meeting agreed that Five roadshows should take place from February to May 2025 in each Municipal District. 
A full meeting will take place on the 19th of September to initiate planning for 2025.   
PLAYFUL STREETS 2024
Playful Streets is a nationwide initiative that encourages children to play outside freely and safely in their local neighbour-
hoods, making exercise fun and easy and in doing so, offers neighbours a chance to meet and build stronger connections 
within their communities.  Healthy Waterford and Waterford Sports Partnership teamed up with key stakeholders for the 
roll out Playful Streets 2024, including Waterford City and County Council Libraries, Ready Steady Play, Sláintecare 
Healthy Communities, Waterford PPN, Community Safety Partnership and CYPSC.  
Throughout this phase of Playful Streets, the organising committee are beginning to rebrand the initiative as it fosters 
more than just play and really brings a sense of connection, community and pride of place to the area. Feedback has been 
very positive and being able to meet local residents on their doorsteps with a positive initiative like this has brought the 
local authority even more connected with local residents. One resident said: “This was one of the best community activities 
I’ve come across. So much fun for both children and adults. We would love this to happen again in 2025!”
This summer, there are over 28 events scheduled to take place within Waterford between the months of May to Septem-
ber, many of which have already taken place. Playful Street events provide a great opportunity for communities to work 
together and training and supports are available to Residents’ Associations / Community Groups who wish to take part. 
For more information about Playful Streets 2024, please contact Eoin Morrissey eoinmorrissey@waterfordcouncil.ie .
BIKE WEEK 2024
National Bike took place from the 11th to the 19th May and saw 3,212 participants of all ages and abilities taking part in 
47 events in Waterford.  Successful events ranged from an E-Bike Guided Cycle, Dawn Cycle, Lunchtime Cycles, RSC 
Schools Festival, Bike Maintenance Workshops, Greenway Cycles, local Schools Events, Mountain Bike Taster Sessions, 
and many other great initiatives

COMMUNITY INTEGRATION FORUM
The Community Integration Forum is in place to assist with supporting and integrating beneficiaries of temporary protec-
tion and international protection (IP) applicants into our communities. All key agencies are working in collaboration with 
the Local Authority Integration Team to provide services and supports to all Ukrainians and IPs arriving to Waterford.  The

Waterford’s Ukrainian rest centres are now closed having accommodated and supported over 2,110 Ukrainians since April 
2022.  Waterford Council currently operate a Designated Accommodation Centre to accommodate and support Ukrainians 
who arrived in Ireland after 14th March 2024, under the 90 Day Accommodation policy.

on an ongoing basis.    Any queries on same should be directed to offerahome@waterfordcouncil.ie or 058 22059.

CLIMATE ACTION
Community Climate Action Fund
16 communities from across the County have commenced their Community Climate projects. Projects varied in size from 
less than €5,000 up to €100,000 and include everything from setting up community orchards to upgrading community 
buildings and providing sustainable travel options.
Retrofit of streetlights to energy efficient equivalents
The Public Lighting Energy Efficiency Project (PLEEP) is moving from the design stage to implementation and by the 
end of the summer the first energy efficient replacement of streetlights will have been completed, reducing the energy 
consumption of our lighting by 70% saving money and carbon emissions.
Smarter Travel Mark
Waterford City and County Council has received the Bronze Smarter Travel Mark from the NTA for the efforts being made 
to give staff more sustainable travel options.
Environmental Education & Awareness
Rubbish Schools Film Festival - The Environment Section worked with Createschool to offer 5 secondary schools in 
Waterford the opportunity to participate in the Rubbish Film. The Rubbish Film Festival is a really unique opportunity for 
Transition Year Students to showcase their creative talents, create awareness on Environmental Issues such as Climate 
Action and learn some new digital storytelling skills in the process. Each participating school received an intensive 2-day 
workshop on-site in their school from Createschool to help them gain and/or develop the skills to create their own short 
ONE MINUTE film or films that will create awareness among their peers on their selected environmental issue. All costs 
are covered by the Environment Section of Waterford City & County Council. A national awards ceremony took place in 
late April for this.

Composting in Schools programme – 8 secondary schools in Co. Waterford took part in a waste prevention and recycling 
programme designed to identify ways for the school to reduce the amount of waste being produced and increase recycling 
and composting. This resulted in 7 of the 8 schools reducing the amount of waste being sent to landfill. 5 of the 8 schools 
signed up for a brown bin collection to compost food waste. 3 leaf cages were installed to compost leaves on school 
grounds and staff and students learned about the importance of waste prevention and recycling. 
Workshops, etc:
Food Waste information days were held at Tramore, Ardkeen, Dungarvan, Portlaw and Kilmacthomas libraries and the 
Age Well Expo. This included an information display, with advice being given on the day about correct waste segregation. 
Over 1000 compost caddies, compostable bags, food measures and information leaflets were distributed to help house-
holders to reduce their food waste and compost.
Connecting Communities Roadshow – The Environment Department took part in the Connecting Communities Roadshow 
at 7 locations around the county this spring. Currently, other partners at the Roadshow include various WCCC depart-
ments, Waterford PPN, Waterford Sports Partnership, Waterford Leader, Waterford Area Partnership, Local Link, HSE 
Health Promotion, Waterford Volunteer Centre, Community Guards, Fire Service and WWETB, with the idea that the 
greater the collaboration, the better the attendance at each roadshow. The Environment Department’s display focussed 
on waste prevention. This has taken place in Lismore, Dungarvan, Ballymacarbry, Tramore, Kilbarry in Waterford and 
Kilmacthomas.
Community Clean-Ups
Waterford City & County Council facilitates community clean ups throughout the year to clean up litter and illegally dumped 
waste from approach roads, local beauty spots, beaches and general public areas. The Environment Department contin-
ue to supply bags, gloves and litter pickers to many of the groups taking part, distributing them from both our Dungarvan 
and Waterford offices. Collection of any bags of litter is then organised for after the clean-up takes place.

The Fountain in the People’s Park was unveiled on 29th May. The new fountain, which has retained the shape and lime-
stone capping of the previous fountain, consists of a 7-metre stainless steel spray ring with 88 individual water jets along 
with a dynamic colour change lighting display and a water filter system that can be monitored and accessed remotely.
